events.title: Vellmark Reserve Authority holds its policy rate at 4.25%
events.takeaway: The hold was expected; dropping the phrase "further tightening" was not.
data_points: Policy rate unchanged at **4.25%** for the fourth meeting in a row
The statement no longer says "further tightening may be appropriate"
Vote was 7-2; both dissenters preferred a 25bp cut
Core inflation forecast for year-end trimmed from 3.1% to 2.8%
events.argument: Markets priced a hold with unchanged guidance. Removing the tightening bias and showing two dissents for a cut moves the debate from whether to cut to when. The inflation forecast trim gives the committee cover, but it rests on a single soft services print.
counterpoints: The governor said twice that the committee is "in no hurry"
Wage growth is still 4.6%, well above what a 2.8% inflation forecast implies

sources.title: Vellmark Reserve Authority policy statement, March 2026

events.title: Calder Street Research: the memory upcycle is a supply story
events.takeaway: Supply growth is halving while demand stays flat, so pricing power comes from discipline, not from a boom.
events.body_md:
#### 1. Core claim and key numbers

Calder Street argues that this memory upcycle is driven by **supply discipline**, not by a demand surge. The numbers it leans on:

| Metric | 2024 | 2025 | 2026E | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Industry bit supply growth | 19% | 11% | 8% | Lowest planned growth in a decade |
| Industry bit demand growth | 14% | 12% | 13% | Roughly flat: no demand boom |
| Inventory at makers (weeks) | 14 | 9 | 6 | Below the 8-week comfort level |
| Contract price change | -22% | +9% | +18% | Pricing follows inventory, with a lag |

The single most important row is the first one: demand barely moves, supply growth more than halves.

#### 2. The logic chain

**Link one: capex went elsewhere.** Makers moved spending from new wafer capacity to packaging and process upgrades, which add far fewer bits per dollar.

**Link two: inventory drained quietly.** With demand growing 12-13% against supply at 8-11%, maker inventory fell from 14 weeks to a projected 6.

**Link three: pricing power returns before volumes do.** Below about 8 weeks of inventory, buyers historically accept contract increases to secure allocation.

#### 3. Side threads that are easy to miss

- The note assumes no new entrant ramps before 2028; one delayed fab is treated as cancelled.
- Packaging capacity, not wafers, is the binding constraint, which links this note to the Northwind capex story.

#### 4. Closing loop

**Less new capacity, steady demand, thinner inventory, then price: the upcycle is a supply story, and it lasts only as long as the discipline does.**
counterpoints: Supply discipline has broken in every previous cycle once prices rose for three quarters
The 2026 demand estimate comes from maker guidance, the same makers who benefit from a tight narrative
The note was published one week before two of the covered companies report, which is convenient timing

sources.title: Calder Street Research: Memory 2026, discipline over demand

events.title: Northwind capex: Quillon Tools confirms an order pull-in
events.takeaway: The first supplier confirmation: Northwind's packaging spend is showing up in order books.
events.what_changed: Quillon Tools says a "large existing customer" moved NWD 1.1bn of packaging-tool orders from the second half into the first.
data_points: Lead time for bonding tools now 11 months, up from 8
events.argument: Yesterday the capex raise was a plan; today part of it is a purchase order. Longer lead times support the reading that packaging is the bottleneck.
counterpoints: A pull-in moves orders forward; it does not by itself make the full-year total larger
